correctness.rationale: The planar cosine-product identity gives one doubled-angle cosine per pair per third vertex. Thus the doubled-spin density has coupling c_N=c(1−2/N) and weight exp(c_N|S_N|²/(2N)); the undoubled signs conditional on all doubled angles are independent and fair. The exact Rademacher fourth moment counts three pairings and corrects the all-equal indices, yielding 2−2/N+|m_N|² conditionally. The second complex moment conditionally equals m_N, whose angular average is zero, so the planar covariance is exactly I/2. An editorial distinction: the formula's baseline 2−2/N is the pairing subtraction, not the actual independent-uniform-spin fourth moment 2−1/N. Relative to the latter the exact excess is E|m_N|²−1/N; the displayed finite-N and critical equations are correct as written. For the radial auxiliary field the likelihood-ratio argument gives strict decrease of I_1(r)/(r I_0(r)) from 1/2 to zero, yielding the stated maximizers; the tail is controlled by log I_0(r)≤r. Conditional log cos gives the planar Fourier exponent −|t|²/4−Re((t_1−it_2)²m_N)/4+O_K(N^−1), uniformly on each compact K. Averaging over the uniform direction and taking the radial concentration limit gives the Bessel mixture, whose fourth-coordinate-moment excess is 3ρ²/2 after standardization. At c=2, with h=N^−1/4 u, the finite-size quadratic shift is O(N^−1/2 |u|²); the log I_0 Taylor remainder is O(N^−1/2 |u|^6). On |h|≤δ both exponents are bounded above by −κ|u|^4 for fixed small δ and κ>0; the difference of their exponentials is controlled by this integrable bound times N^−1/2(|u|²+|u|^6). The complement has exponentially small contribution to the needed moments by the strict free-energy gap and Gaussian tail. The quartic law has E|u|²=8/√π. The exact conditional second moment of the doubled-spin sample mean is 1/N+(1−1/N)(I_1(|h|)/I_0(|h|))², giving E|m_N|²=2/√(πN)+O(N^−1). The conditional independent bounded summands give O(N^−2) fourth moment for the centered sample mean, and the field fourth moment is O(N^−1), hence E|m_N|⁴=O(N^−1). Expanding the angular I_0 factor at |t|²|m_N|/4 now gives |t|⁴/(32√(πN)) with the stated compact-uniform remainder. The supplied quadrature/sign-check code and recorded scope were read, not executed; the amplitudes and remainder were checked analytically.

value.rationale: Because the first harmonic is commonly measured yet its covariance cannot diagnose the transition in this model, knowing exactly which higher-order statistic detects the director is useful. The result also determines when Gaussian modeling of that observable fails, identifies the mixing mechanism, and separates a Gaussian critical limit from its leading non-Gaussian finite-size correction. This is specific to the zero-field canonical law; it makes no claim about noisy measurements, dynamics or ensembles in a field.
